reflection: The team now rests on volume-surge factors (AAPL volume relative to NVDA volume, NVDA volume log, and AAPL volume versus QQQ on a 60-day baseline). They help mostly in 2023 and 2025 and miss in 2022 and 2024, and their gains are small enough that they are hard to tell apart from noise. Several failures share a cause: the signals ignore whether the market moved up or down, and the 20-day baseline gets distorted by spikes. The QQQ overnight gap helps when paired with AAPL volume (4/4 years), so it may be a useful partner. Next I will try regime-scaled versions of the gap and the NVDA volume signal, plus a different Apple-own location signal and a combined peer volume measure.

lessons.name: nvda_volume_surge_log
lessons.lesson: The log NVDA volume surge helped in 2023 and 2025 but missed badly in 2024 because it is direction-blind and the 20-day baseline is spike-sensitive, so it works only as a team partner, not alone.

lessons.name: aapl_volume_surge_vs_nvda_log
lessons.lesson: Taking the log of the AAPL-to-NVDA volume surge tamed the extreme spikes and it helped in 3 of 4 years on the team, but its 2024 miss shows it still lacks a direction signal.

lessons.name: qqq_overnight_gap_1d
lessons.lesson: The QQQ overnight gap is too unstable alone (missed 2022 and 2024) but its pairing with AAPL volume surge helped in all four years, suggesting it captures timing information that the volume factor lacks.

lessons.name: qqq_range_surge
lessons.lesson: Normalising QQQ's daily range by its own 20-day mean carried no next-day direction information and hurt the model in 2022 and 2024, so it was rejected.

lessons.name: aapl_msft_range_ratio
lessons.lesson: AAPL's range relative to MSFT's helped in 2022, 2023 and 2025 but its gain was too small and it overlaps with AAPL's own daily range, so it adds little independent information.

lessons.name: aapl_range_volatility_10d
lessons.lesson: The 10-day standard deviation of Apple's range duplicated the existing volatility factors and hurt the team, so it was rejected.

factors.name: qqq_gap_scaled_by_qqq_vol
factors.hypothesis: The raw QQQ gap was too large in high-volatility regimes (missing in 2022 and 2024), so dividing by QQQ's own 20-day volatility should put the gap on a comparable scale across regimes and make it steadier.

factors.name: nvda_volume_surge_60d_log
factors.hypothesis: The 20-day NVDA baseline is pulled up by recent spikes, causing the 2024 miss; a 60-day baseline should measure abnormal volume against a slower norm and reduce these false surges.

factors.name: msft_overnight_gap_1d
factors.hypothesis: MSFT's overnight gap reflects news that reaches the large-cap tech complex before Apple opens, a different peer timing signal from the QQQ gap.

factors.name: aapl_close_location_1d
factors.hypothesis: Where Apple closed within its daily range shows whether buyers or sellers controlled the last hour, which may carry short-term continuation information.

factors.name: peer_volume_surge_sum
factors.hypothesis: Combined abnormal volume across the two megacap peers measures market-wide participation, which may mark stronger moves in the next session in a way that a single-stock volume signal cannot.

factors.name: aapl_close_loc_with_nvda_volume
factors.formula: multiply(safe_divide(subtract(AAPL_Close, AAPL_Low), subtract(AAPL_High, AAPL_Low)), log(safe_divide(NVDA_Volume, rolling_mean(NVDA_Volume, 20))))
factors.hypothesis: Abnormal NVDA volume carries a direction-blind signal; weighting it by where Apple closed in its range tags the volume with whether buyers or sellers dominated, giving a complementary Apple-own view.

factors.name: aapl_minus_qqq_gap_1d
factors.formula: subtract(safe_divide(subtract(AAPL_Open, lag(AAPL_Close, 1)), lag(AAPL_Close, 1)), safe_divide(subtract(QQQ_Open, lag(QQQ_Close, 1)), lag(QQQ_Close, 1)))
factors.hypothesis: The difference between Apple's and QQQ's overnight gaps isolates Apple-specific overnight news, which should complement the market-level QQQ gap by separating stock-specific from index-wide moves.
